hypotheses.justification: Implied by h. FooteLit.statedClassicalModel_of_lieModel_psl_two h gives StatedClassicalModel X .PSL 2 p f. Its first component is StatedLieAdmissible .PSL 2 p f, which unfolds to p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ f ∧ …. The proof already destructs this with `obtain ⟨-, F, _, _, hcard, ⟨e⟩⟩`, discarding that component. Replacing the `-` by `⟨hp, hf, -⟩` recovers hp, the only place it is used (in `⟨p, f, hp, …⟩`). Nothing else in the statement needs hp, so the theorem is unchanged. This also holds if hf is deleted, but the two deletions share the same obtain pattern.

Implied by h in the same way. The admissibility component StatedLieAdmissible .PSL 2 p f of the StatedClassicalModel obtained from h is p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ f ∧ …. Destructuring it as `⟨hp', hf', -⟩` gives 1 ≤ f for the one use, in `⟨p, f, hp, …, hf, hcard⟩`. The conclusion does not mention hf, so the theorem is still true and provable without it. It can be deleted independently of hp, or together with it.
